standard_prerequisites.name: Empirical frequency vector and Dirichlet limit
standard_prerequisites.statement: delta_{f,x} is the vector of normalised logarithms of the ordered parts of a random factorisation, and Z is the Dirichlet limit vector.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two random vectors whose laws the statement compares.

standard_prerequisites.name: The events E, E_cnt(A) and E_prob(A)
standard_prerequisites.statement: E is the coupling event of the author's coupling lemma; E_cnt(A) and E_prob(A) are the events that the two relevant closed balls avoid the boundary of the measurable set A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement bounds the discrepancy by the complements of these events plus 1/log x, and the proof works on their intersection.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coupling distance bound
standard_prerequisites.statement: On the coupling event E one has a uniform bound on the maximal norm of the difference of delta_{f,x} and Z, in terms of log(x/N_x), log s(N_x) and Theta_x.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the radius within which a point of the connecting segment is exhibited.

core_obligations: Reduce the claimed O-bound to the deterministic stronger statement that on E and E_cnt(A) and E_prob(A), membership of delta_{f,x} in A is equivalent to membership of Z in A (source lines 1274-1279).

Assume delta_{f,x} in A and Z not in A, define the radius R_nt' from the logarithm of x/N_x and of s(N_x), and use the transition estimate to place the ball of radius R_nt' around delta_{f,x}^* inside the corresponding ball around delta_{f,x} (source lines 1283-1287).

Use the two avoidance assumptions to place the balls around delta_{f,x} and around Z respectively inside A and inside its complement; since both are convex, a point on the segment joining delta_{f,x} to Z lies in both, a contradiction (source lines 1287-1295).
Obtain the converse direction by the symmetric variation of the same argument (source line 1297).

proof_roadmap.step: Pass from the integral estimate to a deterministic implication on the intersection of the three events.
Contradiction through convexity of the unit simplex and of the two balls, using the coupling distance bound to put a point of the connecting segment in the intersection.
Repeat the argument with the roles of delta_{f,x} and Z exchanged.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1266-1272: for every measurable subset A of the simplex, the probability that the empirical frequency vector lies in A differs from the probability that the Dirichlet limit lies in A by O(measure of the complements of the two exception events plus 1/log x). The proof (source lines 1274-1298) does not estimate the two probabilities separately but proves the stronger deterministic statement that on the intersection of the three events the two membership conditions coincide. The forward direction is a contradiction argument: one places a ball of an explicit radius around the empirical vector inside A and a ball around the limit inside the complement, uses the coupling distance bound to exhibit a point on the segment joining the two centres, and concludes by convexity of the simplex and of the two balls; the reverse direction is the symmetric variation of the same argument. Neither the deterministic reduction nor the convexity step appears in the statement.
